name: rifts
title: Rift schedule: the server read, the re-push, and the sixty-second heartbeat

steps.note: Evidence 203 (FRIFT1). The '.rifts' STATUS reply is chat-only and a ghost has no chat slot, so the reply lines themselves still owe a real user - what is scriptable, and what evidence 203 actually measured on the server, is the broadcast line: the schedule read off WarEventSystem, sent on join/change and then exactly every sixty seconds. recipients=0 with nobody connected is the expected value, not a failure.
'.rifts send' is SendToUser, deliberately not a broadcast. A ghost has no connection, so sent=false and recipients=0; the line is written either way and carries the freshly read schedule.

steps.expectLog: Sample rifts: sent SmRf to user \d+ recipients=\d+ reason=change v\d+ T1\[.+\] T2\[.+\] nextType=\S+ utc=\d+

steps.note: Sixty-five seconds: one heartbeat has to land inside it (evidence 203 measured the gap at exactly 60 s).

steps.expectLog: Sample rifts: sent SmRf to all recipients=\d+ reason=heartbeat v\d+ T1\[.+\] T2\[.+\] nextType=\S+ utc=\d+

steps.expectNoLog: Sample rifts: ignored an SmRf packet
